  <span style="color: grey; font-weight: 700; font-size: 40px;">elgin akin</span>
  
  <p>Hi, I'm Elgin. I am a 5th year PhD candidate in the <a href="https://pekoszlab.com">Pekosz Lab</a> at the <a href="https://publichealth.jhu.edu/">Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health</a> in <a href="https://publichealth.jhu.edu/departments/molecular-microbiology-and-immunology">Molecular Microbiology and Immunology</a>. I investigate the evolutionary dynamics of influenza viruses, focusing on how mutations influence both _in vitro_ fitness, host response and immune escape. Additionally, I maintain <a href="https://nextstrain.org/groups/PekoszLab-Public"> several nextstrain builds</a> for seasonal genomic surveillance of H1N1, H3N2 and Influenza B viruses from patients in the Johns Hopkins Hospital Network. </p>
